I'm glad. As a pretty new fan of comic books, the whole of the art seems like a giant tidal wave. You either pick your spot and dive in, or it's gonna chew you up. I don't really understand the obsession with a universe-wide continuity. There's just too many characters and too much stuff happening to fit it all together in a neat little package. Sometimes I wish there was a universal continuity featuring all the characters, and another one where individual characters were the ONLY superheroes in their own universe. Like a world with ONLY a Batman and nothing else (except, maybe, his sidekicks) and one with ONLY a Superman, etc. Then again, what do I know.

I feel the same way with all of the multiversal stuff most of the time, but I the way I see it is without the concept of the multiverse we would have any of the amazing elseworlds stories like Superman Red Son or Kingdom Come. But when it comes to the main continuity and having only one superhero at a time, I really like that idea but maybe only as a one shot or something like that, I feel like over time only featuring one superhero would get boring. Also I live for interactions between Superman and Batman for example, or GL and Green Arrow.

Oh, don't get me wrong. I love the multiverse concept. For instance, I like the Earth One books that allow writers the freedom to alter things without upsetting the main continuity. Ideally, there would be enough 'verses to encompass any possibility a writer wished to explore. And it's cool when those universes spill into each other and you have multiples of every character interacting, but it does tend to get messy after a while to hold all that together. I kind of like how Grant Morrison seems to have his own personal continuity that remains consistent regardless of whatever else is happening. I'm no expert though, not yet, anyway. I've read about instances when certain characters were made unavailable at times to certain writers because someone was doing something with them elsewhere. I'd prefer it if the creators had the freedom to tell their stories without having to worry about screwing things up. Like, we have The Dark Knight Returns and Kingdom Come, both dealing with older Supermans and Batmans interacting in totally different ways. It's not hard to carry both those versions of events in one's head without one needing to be canon. To me what's confusing is trying to fit disparate characters that rarely, or never, interact in books with widely differing tones into one all-encompassing set of events. Anyway, these are just my thoughts after getting into [DC] comics in my 30s and coming across all these various reboots and re-imaginings. Thanks for replying. Maybe someday you can explain (in a way I can understand) what the hell is going on in Final Crisis. ;)
